messages:
Maria L: Heads-up — getting 5 separate customer escalations about p95/p99 latency for text-generation API in us-west-2 since ~10:12 PST. p95 jumped ~180ms -> ~1.2s, p99 up to ~2.8s. No spike in 5xxs, just slow tails. Tickets: INC-4121, INC-4123, INC-4127. Can someone triage? @Jon P @Sean H :rotating_light:

infra-bot: Alert: p95_latency_us-west2_textgen > 500ms for 5m (rule: p95>500ms).

support-bot: Related customer notes: multiple long-running responses from large-model route, some mention truncated outputs when client times out.

Jon P: On it. First quick checks: any recent deploys to serving runtime / model variants in us-west-2 in last 2 hours? Also check autoscaler, GPU queue length, pod restarts, and model-specific kernel/compiler logs.

Alex W: No infra deploys from me. There was a model reconfiguration pushed by model-onboard team at 09:58 — swapped default variant of `redwood/gpt-large-v2` to `-v2-quant`. Might be related.

Sean H: ok checklist I'm running:
- kube top pod cpu/gpu util for us-west serving nodes
- `kubectl get pods -l app=serving-us-west -o wide`
- check redis/KV cache hit rate (prefix cache)
- check batcher queue length and batch latencies

Jon P: grabbing traces. Can we repro quickly with a deterministic sample? Maria, do you have a sample request-id from a slow request?

Maria L: Yep attached in ticket INC-4123: request-id `req_20260315_83b9`. I tried the curl locally and saw ~1.9s on 3/5 runs. Repro is intermittent but consistent on certain payloads (longer context + streaming enabled).

Alex W: sharing a quick trace snippet from the runtime logs for that req: (cleaned)
```
[2026-03-15T10:18:02Z] req_20260315_83b9 start -> route=textgen-large
[2026-03-15T10:18:02Z] model_load_check -> variant=v2-quant, quant_path=fp8
[2026-03-15T10:18:02Z] kv_cache_lookup -> miss
[2026-03-15T10:18:02Z] batcher_enqueue -> waiting for batch (current_size=1)
[2026-03-15T10:18:03Z] kernel_compile_time=0.93s
[2026-03-15T10:18:04Z] generate_tokens start -> latency=1.12s total
```
Looks like a kernel/compile spike on first requests for that variant.

Sean H: hmm kernel_compile_time ~0.9s is bad for p99. If quant path triggers a one-off compile, it can tank p95/p99 for a subset of traffic until warm. But we saw sustained high p95 across the board, not just first-request. Need to check how many pods warmed and whether autoscaler spun new pods with cold caches.

Jon P: Agreed. Immediate mitigations we can try now (quick playbook):
1) circuit-breaker: fallback to `redwood/gpt-medium` for that route in us-west when p95>500ms for 2m.
2) reduce default `max_tokens` to 128 for inbound requests to limit generation cost/latency for now.
3) apply per-customer rate limits for heavy tenants (50rps) and global soft cap.
4) route 15-25% of traffic to us-east as temporary load-shed.
5) set batcher max wait to 8ms to prefer latency over throughput.

Alex W: I can push the circuit-breaker + fallback. Suggested circuit-breaker config (quick):
```json
{
  "trigger": {"metric": "p95_latency", "threshold_ms": 500, "window_s": 120},
  "action": {"type": "fallback", "target_model": "redwood/gpt-medium-v1", "duration_s": 600},
  "backoff": {"type": "linear", "step_s": 60}
}
```

Jon P: also run this CLI to quickly reduce tokens and cutoff large requests (run as admin):
```
redwoodctl route update --route textgen-large --set max_tokens=128 --set batcher.max_wait_ms=8
```

Maria L: please also throttle any observed heavy API keys. Tickets list top 3 noisy keys.

Jon P: applying fallback and circuit breaker now...

infra-bot: Action logged by Jon P: route update applied to textgen-large (fallback -> redwood/gpt-medium-v1), circuit-breaker enabled.

Jon P: Pushed, verified rollback point. Confirming metrics...

(2m later) Jon P: Early results: p95 dropped to ~330ms after fallback and batcher change, p99 down from 2.8s -> ~650ms. Token utilization down ~18%. Some customers report slightly different output quality (expected).

Maria L: Nice. Please keep fallback active and we'll notify customers with mitigation note. Also open RCA.

Sean H: Immediate TODOs for post-incident:
- run a model variant warmup job to precompile kernels if we roll that quant variant (infra/serving team)
- add guardrail: auto-fallback rule when p95>500ms for 5m (config + doc)
- add a canary traffic test to deploy model variant to 2 pods before promoting to all
- add metric to detect sustained kernel_compile_time > 200ms across pods

Alex W: Added runbook snippet to the incident ticket for warmup: a background job to do 20 short prompts per pod on startup for each new variant to prime kernel caches.

Jon P: Longer-term changes (to RFC):
- SLO guardrails: default auto-fallback to smaller model when p95 exceeds threshold for X minutes. Make threshold and window configurable per-customer tier.
- Circuit-breaker templates: prebuilt configs (threshold+fallback) that can be attached to routes at creation time.
- Per-tenant backpressure: dynamic token-cost based throttling for heavy users.

Maria L: Assignments: Jon -> open RFC for guardrails + implement template. Alex -> implement warmup job + add to model onboarding. Sean -> update runbook with playbook (including exact CLI commands and escalation path). I'll draft the customer mitigation comms.

Jon P: Opening follow-ups now. RFC draft ticket: RFC-5783. Warmup ticket: INFRA-2209. Runbook update: DOC-3344.

Maria L: thanks everyone. We'll keep the fallback for 1h while monitoring, then consider a staged re-roll of the quant variant with warmup.

support-bot: Noted — customer comms sent for affected tickets with mitigation details and ETA for next update.

Sean H: Quick note for postmortem: root cause timeline likely = model variant promoted without warmup -> first wave of traffic hit cold kernel compiles -> autoscaler reacted by creating more pods (cold) -> sustained tail latency until warmup / fallback.

Maria L: Good summary. Closing the incident channel when we have stable metrics for 30m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
